overview: White develops the bishop to c4 and aims at f7, keeping f4 and Nf3 in reserve. Black chooses between 3...Nxe4 (the wild Frankenstein-Dracula after 4.Qh5), 3...Bc5, which is an Italian-like game after Nf3, and 3...Nc6, which transposes to the Three Knights type. I am unsure which branch strong players choose most, so I read the quiet 3...Bc5 4.Nf3 d6 line.

white_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with Nf3, d3 and O-O, aiming at f7 and keeping f4 for later.
Strike in the centre with f4 or d4 if Black allows.

black_ideas.idea: Mirror White with ...Bc5 and ...d6 and equalise comfortably.
Hit e4 early with ...Nxe4 for sharp play.

typical_structures.structure: Italian-style centre with e4 and d3 against e5 and d6, flexible.

character.notes: Quiet main lines, with a sharp wildcard in the Frankenstein-Dracula. Balanced.

gambit.notes: Main lines do not give material; 3...Nxe4 sacrifices are in a sub-branch.

approach.notes: Vienna Game is standard per the anchors.
